selection_rule: Every statement by an in-scope officeholder quoted in a story published on Nov. 25 or 26, 2026 in the NPR Politics and PBS NewsHour Politics feeds, as read on Nov. 26 at 8:17 a.m. ET, less the stories earlier pages already used, plus every transcript from the fixed transcript sources dated in that window (one was: a White House statement of Nov. 25, which quoted no officeholder in scope). PBS NewsHour carries Associated Press reporting. Three NPR stories (on the Puerto Rico power grid, the proposed tariffs and Sen. Tim Kaine's view of them) returned no readable text and could not be used. Transcripts from Nov. 19 to 24 were searched only to confirm quotes; none held any of the day's quotes. Four of the thirteen readable stories quoted no officeholder in scope. Greetings, quotes under five words, questions, a multi-signer letter, commentators' and reporters' accounts of what officials said, reporters' paraphrases of opinions, and statements by people outside the offices in scope (including the first lady, a lieutenant governor, a state senator, the FCC chair and the trade representative) were left out. Statements are worded as the outlet reported them.
lede: Coverage on Nov. 25 and 26 included the reaction in Congress to Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia's chief executive, a push by some Senate Democrats to add a freshman senator to the party's leadership, Kilmar Ábrego García's departure from the U.S. for Spain, a State Department asylum report, a Georgia court order on Fulton County's 2020 election records, and Vice President JD Vance's Thanksgiving visit to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio.

The page lists 17 statements by 8 officeholders. Six are factual claims; their checks are listed below as they return. The other 11 are opinions, predictions or promises and are listed without a check.

statements.speaker: Brian Fitzpatrick
statements.context: Speaking on NPR's Morning Edition about Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's return as CEO and his coming appearance before House lawmakers, Fitzpatrick, a House Intelligence Committee member, described public concern.
statements.quote: The public is rightly concerned, and they deserve answers

statements.speaker: Brian Fitzpatrick
statements.context: On NPR's Morning Edition, Fitzpatrick described how an investigation of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's ties to China should proceed ahead of Huang's House appearance.
statements.quote: Anytime you do an investigation, you follow the facts wherever they lead, and you report those facts with unimpeachable integrity

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: As reported by NPR on Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's return as CEO, Trump said he helped arrange it.
statements.quote: Reported as: Trump has said he helped arrange Huang's return as CEO, and Nvidia's board maintains that his reinstatement presents no national security risk.
statements.test: True if Nvidia, a board member or another primary record confirms the president took part in arranging Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO, for example by speaking with the board before it acted. False if Nvidia or a board member states on record that the president had no role. Cannot be determined if no primary account of the board's contacts is available.
statements.finding: As reported by CBS News, the president told CNBC he spoke to the board and "convinced them." Nvidia's Nov. 23 release says only that the board received "input from senior levels of the United States government"; no Nvidia or board statement on record confirms or denies his role.

evidence.label: CBS News, Trump says he spoke to Nvidia board
NPR transcript, lawmakers seek answers as Nvidia CEO returns (Nov. 25, 2026)

statements.context: Speaking at a conference of Democrats after the midterm elections, Slotkin described what voters wanted from party leadership.
statements.quote: On election night, people voted very clearly for a new generation of leadership. That was very, very clear

statements.speaker: Cory Booker
statements.context: Booker told MS NOW that Senate Democratic leadership extends beyond the top post, and that he wants incoming senators Annie Andrews and James Talarico to play prominent roles.

statements.speaker: Chris Van Hollen
statements.context: Responding to Kilmar Abrego Garcia leaving the U.S. for Spain, Van Hollen, who met him in El Salvador last year, described the Trump administration's decision to send him to the CECOT prison.
statements.quote: They wanted to leave him to rot there, to rot there for the rest of his life

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: In a post on X after Kilmar Abrego Garcia left the U.S. for Spain, Mullin said he was delighted and listed allegations against him, including gang membership, which Abrego Garcia denies.
statements.quote: Reported as: U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a post on X that he was "delighted" about Ábrego García's departure, listing a familiar litany of allegations for why he should be deported, including that he was a gang member, an accusation that Ábrego García has repeatedly denied.
statements.test: True if a court record or official adjudication (a conviction or a judicial finding) establishes that Kilmar Ábrego García was a member of MS-13 or another gang. False if a court found on the record that he was not a gang member. Cannot be determined if the record holds only allegations, such as a 2019 police gang field interview sheet, with no court deciding the point.
statements.finding: No conviction or court finding read in this check establishes that Ábrego García was a gang member: the May 22, 2026 order dismissing his Tennessee criminal case makes no finding either way, and prosecutors' appeal is pending. The D. Md. docket and the June 2025 detention ruling could not be read directly.

evidence.label: NPR, judge dismisses criminal charges against Ábrego García (May 22, 2026)

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: Speaking at a 2018 White House appearance during his first term, as recounted by the AP, Trump described the purpose of asylum.
statements.quote: Asylum is a very special protection intended only for those fleeing government persecution based on race, religion and other protected status
statements.test: True if U.S. asylum law (8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(42) and 1158) limits asylum to people persecuted, or with a well-founded fear of persecution, on account of race, religion, nationality, membership in a particular social group or political opinion. False if the law grants asylum on other grounds, such as poverty or general violence. Cannot be determined if the point turns on whether 'government persecution' covers the law's protection against persecutors the government cannot or will not control, a legal reading.
statements.finding: 8 U.S.C. 1158(b)(1) and 1101(a)(42)(A), read from AskAmerica's U.S. Code table, limit asylum to persecution or a well-founded fear of it on account of race, religion, nationality, membership in a particular social group or political opinion; poverty is not a ground. The statute does not say the persecutor must be the government, so whether "government persecution" fits the law turns on a legal reading.

evidence.label: law.usc_sections (8 U.S.C. 1101, refugee definition)
evidence.sql: SELECT substr(section_text, position('well-founded fear of persecution on account of' IN section_text) - 200, 900) AS t FROM law.usc_sections WHERE title_number = 8 AND section_number = '1101'

evidence.label: law.usc_sections (8 U.S.C. 1158, asylum)
evidence.sql: SELECT * FROM law.usc_sections WHERE title_number = 8 AND section_number IN ('1158') FETCH FIRST 3 ROWS ONLY

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: In his first term, as recounted by the AP, Trump said most migrants seeking asylum were fleeing poverty.
statements.quote: Reported as: Most asylum seekers, the Republican president said, were fleeing poverty.
statements.test: True if official asylum data or a primary survey from 2017 to 2019 shows a majority of asylum seekers left their countries chiefly for economic reasons. False if such data show most cited persecution or violence as the main reason. Cannot be determined if no primary source measures the motives of asylum seekers as a whole; grant or denial rates alone do not decide it.
statements.finding: The immigration courts' statistics show asylum applications filed (146,165 in fiscal 2017, 165,975 in 2018, 216,745 in 2019) but do not record why applicants left their countries. No primary source read in this check measures asylum seekers' motives as a whole; DHS statistics pages could not be read.

evidence.label: EOIR Adjudication Statistics, total asylum applications

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: As reported by the AP, Trump promised in early 2025, as his immigration crackdown ramped up, to deport 1 million people annually.
statements.quote: Reported as: Ábrego García's deportation in early 2025 came as Trump, a Republican, was ramping up his immigration crackdown, promising to deport 1 million people annually.

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: As reported by the AP on Melania Trump's reunification of children in the Russia-Ukraine war, the president had vowed to broker a quick end to the conflict.
statements.quote: Reported as: Her husband, President Donald Trump, had vowed to broker a quick end to the conflict but has said it's been harder than he expected.

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: As reported by the AP on a Georgia court order over Fulton County's 2020 election records, Trump has insisted voter fraud in the county cost him the state.
statements.quote: Reported as: Trump has consistently insisted without evidence that widespread voter fraud in the county cost him victory in the state.
statements.test: True if Georgia's certified 2020 results, its statewide hand-count audit and recount, or an official investigation found fraud in Fulton County large enough to exceed Joe Biden's statewide margin of about 11,779 votes. False if those official records found no fraud near that size and nothing pending could change them. Cannot be determined if the official records cannot be read, or if an open inquiry could still change the record.
statements.finding: Biden's 2020 Georgia margin was 11,779 votes in AskAmerica's state returns. Georgia's Fulton County investigation report (SEB2023-025, April 2024) and the county's Performance Review Board found no evidence of fraud that would have affected the result, and said the hand-count audit and recount confirmed it; the FBI's inquiry into the seized Fulton records and the State Election Board's effort to reopen its case remain open.

evidence.label: officials.presidential_state_returns (Georgia, 2020)
evidence.sql: SELECT candidate, SUM(candidate_votes) AS votes FROM officials.presidential_state_returns WHERE "year" = 2020 AND state_name = 'Georgia' AND candidate IN ('BIDEN, JOSEPH R. JR','TRUMP, DONALD J.') GROUP BY candidate

evidence.label: Georgia SOS Investigations Division, Fulton County Tabulator Results 2020 (SEB2023-025) and Fulton Performance Review Board report, filed in N.D. Ga. 1:26-cv-00809, Doc. 30-1
NPR, FBI affidavit and State Election Board findings (Feb. 10, 2026)
